title: Independence from Portugal — Aristides Pereira President
description: Cabo Verde achieved independence from Portugal on 5 July 1975 after the Carnation Revolution in Lisbon, with Aristides Pereira of the African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cabo Verde (PAIGC) becoming the first president. The new state inherited a drought-stricken archipelago of nine inhabited islands with a population heavily dependent on remittances from a diaspora that nearly equalled those resident at home.

title: Single-Party PAIGC Rule Established
description: The PAIGC consolidated power as the sole legal party, governing both Cabo Verde and Guinea-Bissau under a unified vision pioneered by the assassinated leader Amílcar Cabral. Pereira and Prime Minister Pedro Pires built a centralised one-party state oriented toward African socialism and non-alignment.

title: Severe Drought Hits the Archipelago
description: A severe Sahelian drought devastated agriculture across the islands, deepening reliance on food aid from international donors and remittances from the diaspora in Portugal, the United States and the Netherlands. Drought-resistance and food security became central concerns of state planning.

title: Guinea-Bissau Coup Ends Planned Union
description: The November 1980 coup in Guinea-Bissau by João Bernardo Vieira against President Luís Cabral broke the planned political union between Bissau and Praia, leaving Cabo Verde diplomatically isolated within the joint PAIGC project. Pereira's government condemned the coup and began rethinking the binational arrangement.

title: PAICV Splits from PAIGC — New Republican Constitution
description: In January 1981 the Cabo Verdean wing renamed itself the African Party for the Independence of Cabo Verde (PAICV), formally severing organisational ties with Guinea-Bissau. A new constitution was promulgated that year codifying the separate Cabo Verdean republic under PAICV one-party rule.

title: Pereira Re-elected by National Assembly
description: President Aristides Pereira was re-elected for a second term by the People's National Assembly under the single-party system. His government pursued a non-aligned foreign policy, strong ties with Lusophone Africa, and gradual diversification away from agricultural dependence.

title: Land Reform Programme Launched
description: The PAICV government implemented a land reform programme aimed at redistributing absentee-owned holdings to tenant farmers and reducing rural inequality inherited from the colonial period. The reforms were modest in scale given Cabo Verde's limited arable land but politically symbolic.

title: Pereira Re-elected for Third Term
description: Aristides Pereira was confirmed for a third presidential term by the single-party assembly, while the economy continued to depend on remittances, food aid and limited fisheries exports. The PAICV maintained a comparatively pragmatic and non-repressive single-party rule by regional standards.

title: PAICV Endorses Multiparty Reform
description: Under domestic and international pressure following the end of the Cold War, the PAICV congress voted in February 1990 to abandon the one-party monopoly and open the political system to competing parties. The constitutional amendment paved the way for the founding of opposition formations including the Movement for Democracy (MpD).

title: First Multiparty Elections — MpD Wins Landslide
description: The Movement for Democracy (MpD) led by Carlos Veiga won a sweeping victory in January 1991 legislative elections, ending sixteen years of PAICV rule. António Mascarenhas Monteiro defeated Pereira in the February presidential ballot, completing what observers called one of Africa's earliest peaceful democratic alternations of power.

title: Carlos Veiga Becomes Prime Minister
description: MpD leader Carlos Veiga took office as prime minister in April 1991, launching a programme of economic liberalisation, privatisation of state enterprises and opening to private foreign investment. The Veiga government realigned Cabo Verde toward closer ties with Portugal, the European Community and the United States.

title: Democratic Constitution Promulgated
description: A new constitution was adopted in September 1992 codifying multiparty democracy, separation of powers, an independent judiciary and a comprehensive bill of rights. The document remains the foundation of the Second Republic and has been amended only modestly since.

title: Privatisation and Economic Liberalisation Programme
description: The Veiga government accelerated privatisation of state-owned banks, utilities and shipping, courted IMF and World Bank support, and removed price controls in an effort to integrate the archipelago into the global economy. The strategy emphasised tourism, light manufacturing and offshore services as growth pillars.

title: Cabo Verde Joins Community of Portuguese Speaking Countries
description: Cabo Verde was a founding member when the Community of Portuguese Speaking Countries (CPLP) was established at the Lisbon summit in 1996, building on preparatory accords from 1995 that anchored Praia inside a Lusophone diplomatic framework spanning four continents. Membership gave the archipelago disproportionate diplomatic weight relative to its size.

title: Veiga Re-elected — MpD Wins Second Mandate
description: The MpD won a second consecutive landslide in December 1995 legislative elections, with Carlos Veiga continuing as prime minister, while Mascarenhas Monteiro was returned unopposed to the presidency in February 1996. The smooth re-election cemented Cabo Verde's reputation as one of Africa's most stable democracies.

title: Escudo Pegged to Portuguese Escudo via Cooperation Accord
description: Cabo Verde signed an exchange-rate cooperation agreement with Portugal in March 1998 that pegged the Cabo Verdean escudo to the Portuguese escudo and, on Portugal's adoption of the euro, to the euro at a fixed rate. The peg has anchored monetary stability and tamed inflation for more than two decades.

title: Veiga Resigns to Run for Presidency
description: Carlos Veiga stepped down as prime minister in mid-2000 to contest the upcoming presidential election, handing the premiership to Gualberto do Rosário. The succession exposed strains within the MpD ahead of the 2001 polls.

title: PAICV Returns to Power — Pires President, Neves Prime Minister
description: The PAICV won the January 2001 legislative elections under José Maria Neves, who became prime minister, while Pedro Pires narrowly defeated Carlos Veiga in the February presidential ballot. The peaceful second alternation of power confirmed the maturity of the country's democracy.

title: Tourism Master Plan Targets Sal and Boa Vista
description: The Pires-Neves government adopted a national tourism master plan that prioritised large-scale resort development on the eastern islands of Sal and Boa Vista, attracting significant Spanish, Portuguese and Italian foreign direct investment. Tourism would grow from a marginal sector to the leading source of foreign exchange within a decade.

title: Special Cooperation Agreement with the European Union
description: Cabo Verde signed an enhanced cooperation framework with the European Union providing development financing, fisheries access in exchange for compensation, and preparatory steps toward a deeper political and economic partnership. The EU became the country's dominant external partner.

title: Millennium Challenge Account Compact Signed
description: The United States and Cabo Verde signed a five-year, US$110 million Millennium Challenge Compact in July 2005 funding port modernisation, watershed management and private-sector reform. The award reflected Cabo Verde's reputation for good governance and was renewed in a second compact a few years later.

title: PAICV Wins Re-election — Pires and Neves Continue
description: The PAICV narrowly won the January 2006 legislative elections, returning José Maria Neves as prime minister, and Pedro Pires defeated Carlos Veiga again in the February presidential ballot. Continuity allowed sustained pursuit of tourism-led growth and graduation from least-developed status.

title: UN Graduates Cabo Verde from Least Developed Country Status
description: The United Nations General Assembly voted on 13 December 2007 to graduate Cabo Verde from Least Developed Country status, making it only the second country ever to do so after Botswana. The graduation, effective in 2008, recognised steady gains in income, human capital and economic vulnerability indicators despite continuing structural fragilities.

title: Cabo Verde Accedes to the World Trade Organization
description: Cabo Verde formally joined the World Trade Organization on 23 July 2008 after years of accession negotiations, locking in trade liberalisation commitments and signalling its strategic commitment to integration into the global economy. WTO membership coincided with the LDC graduation.

title: Special Partnership with the European Union
description: The European Union and Cabo Verde launched a Special Partnership in November 2007 that was operationalised through 2008, covering security, mobility, regional integration, knowledge society, technical and normative convergence with EU rules. It is the EU's only such partnership with a small West African state.

title: Global Financial Crisis Hits Tourism and Remittances
description: The global financial crisis cut deeply into European tourist arrivals and diaspora remittances, exposing the archipelago's exposure to external shocks even as growth remained positive overall. The downturn slowed planned investment in resort developments on Sal and Boa Vista.

title: Cabeolica Wind Farm Inaugurated
description: The Cabeolica project, a public-private partnership inaugurated in 2011-2012 across four islands, brought 25.5 MW of wind power on line and supplied around a quarter of the country's electricity at peak. The flagship development positioned Cabo Verde as a continental leader in renewable integration despite small-grid challenges.

title: PAICV Wins Third Mandate — Fonseca President
description: The PAICV under José Maria Neves narrowly won the February 2011 legislative elections, but the MpD-backed Jorge Carlos Fonseca won the August presidential ballot. The cohabitation between a PAICV government and an MpD-aligned head of state proved workable.

title: Second Millennium Challenge Compact Signed
description: The United States signed a second five-year Millennium Challenge Compact with Cabo Verde valued at US$66 million, focused on land management reform and water and sanitation. Cabo Verde was one of the first countries to receive a second MCC compact, reflecting strong governance scorecards.

title: NATO Steadfast Cobalt Exercise Hosted
description: Cabo Verde hosted elements of NATO's Steadfast Cobalt 2013 exercise, an interoperability event that underscored the archipelago's strategic location on Atlantic sea lanes between Europe, Africa and the Americas. The hosting reflected Praia's preference for engagement with Western security partners.

title: Mobility Partnership and Visa Facilitation with the EU
description: Cabo Verde and the European Union deepened their mobility partnership in 2014 with a visa facilitation and readmission agreement, easing short-stay travel for Cabo Verdean citizens to the Schengen area. The deal was unique among African states and reflected the special partnership framework.

title: Pico do Fogo Eruption Devastates Chã das Caldeiras
description: The Pico do Fogo volcano on Fogo island erupted on 23 November 2014, with lava flows destroying the villages of Portela and Bangaeira inside the Chã das Caldeiras caldera and displacing the entire community of around a thousand residents. The eruption continued into February 2015, causing tens of millions of dollars in damage.

title: Severe Drought Stresses Agriculture and Water Supply
description: A multi-year drought intensified across the archipelago, sharply reducing rainfed cereal production, straining municipal water supplies and forcing emergency desalination expansion. The episode highlighted Cabo Verde's acute vulnerability to climate variability and motivated investment in water security.

title: MpD Returns to Power — Correia e Silva Prime Minister
description: The Movement for Democracy under Ulisses Correia e Silva won the March 2016 legislative elections, ending fifteen years of PAICV rule, while Jorge Carlos Fonseca was re-elected president in October. The third peaceful alternation of power further entrenched democratic norms.

title: Lobito Corridor and Belt and Road Engagement
description: Cabo Verde formally joined China's Belt and Road Initiative through a 2018 memorandum of understanding building on engagement begun in 2017, while exploring logistical roles linked to the Lobito Corridor connecting Angola to the Atlantic. Chinese financing supported port and connectivity projects across the archipelago.

title: Drought Returns and Triggers Emergency Plan
description: Rains failed across most of the archipelago for a second consecutive year, prompting the government to launch a drought contingency plan with food assistance, livestock destocking subsidies and accelerated investment in desalination. Recurrent drought reinforced strategic prioritisation of climate adaptation.

title: National Renewable Energy Target Raised to 50 percent
description: The Correia e Silva government revised national energy planning to target a 50 percent renewable share of electricity generation by 2030, scaling up wind and solar additions and pilot battery storage projects. The plan built on Cabeolica and the existing 25 percent renewable share.

title: Tourism Surpasses 700,000 Annual Arrivals
description: International tourist arrivals exceeded 700,000 in 2018, more than the country's resident population of around 540,000, with Sal and Boa Vista accounting for the bulk of beach package traffic from European source markets. Tourism became the dominant driver of GDP growth, employment and foreign exchange.

title: Cabo Verde Targets 100 percent Sustainable Energy by 2040
description: Cabo Verde launched a long-term roadmap presented at international climate fora aiming for 100 percent renewable electricity by 2040, supported by partnerships with the European Union, Germany and the African Development Bank. The ambition reinforced the country's positioning as a small-island climate leader.

title: COVID-19 Pandemic Devastates Tourism Economy
description: The COVID-19 pandemic abruptly halted international air links in March 2020, collapsing tourist arrivals by more than 70 percent and triggering the deepest recession in Cabo Verde's modern history with GDP contracting around 14 percent. Government emergency support to firms and households relied heavily on multilateral budget support.

title: Pandemic-Driven Economic Recession
description: The collapse in tourism, remittances and FDI tipped the economy into the worst contraction on record, pushing public debt above 140 percent of GDP and requiring an IMF Rapid Credit Facility disbursement. The shock exposed the vulnerability of the tourism-led growth model.

title: MpD Wins Second Mandate — Correia e Silva Continues
description: The MpD under Ulisses Correia e Silva won the April 2021 legislative elections with a comfortable majority despite the pandemic recession, validating the government's emergency management. Election observers from the African Union and CPLP described the polls as free, fair and transparent.

title: José Maria Neves Elected President
description: Former PAICV prime minister José Maria Neves won the October 2021 presidential election in the first round with around 51 percent of the vote, defeating MpD-backed candidate Carlos Veiga. The result restored cohabitation between an MpD government and a PAICV head of state.

title: Alex Saab Extradition to the United States
description: Cabo Verdean authorities extradited Colombian-Venezuelan businessman Alex Saab to the United States in October 2021 after more than a year of detention in Praia following his 2020 arrest under a US warrant. The case strained relations with Caracas and provoked sustained diplomatic and legal controversy.

title: Drought and Food Insecurity Spike
description: A renewed multi-year drought combined with global food and fuel price shocks following Russia's invasion of Ukraine pushed an estimated 15 percent of the population into food insecurity. The government extended emergency cash transfers, food vouchers and subsidised water deliveries to inland communities.

title: Tourism Recovery Begins as Restrictions Lift
description: International tourist arrivals rebounded sharply once European pandemic restrictions were lifted in 2022, returning to roughly 70 percent of pre-pandemic peaks and pulling growth above 15 percent year on year. The recovery was concentrated in Sal and Boa Vista beach resorts.

title: Public Debt Restructuring and IMF Programme
description: The government concluded a new IMF Extended Credit Facility programme in 2022-2023 worth around US$60 million to anchor fiscal consolidation, reduce public debt and rebuild reserves after the pandemic shock. The programme set out a multi-year glide path back to debt sustainability.

title: Drought Persists into Sixth Year in Some Islands
description: Several islands recorded their sixth consecutive failed rainy season, with São Nicolau and Santo Antão particularly affected by collapsed rainfed agriculture. The government accelerated rollout of large-scale solar-powered desalination capacity.

title: Air Connectivity Restored as Tourism Surpasses Pre-Pandemic Peak
description: Tourist arrivals surpassed the 2019 record in 2024 as European carriers and charter operators restored or expanded routes to Sal, Boa Vista and Santiago, with around one million arrivals. Tourism returned to its position as the dominant engine of growth and employment.

title: Drought Emergency Continues into Tenth Consecutive Year
description: The government declared continuing drought emergency measures across Santiago, Fogo and Maio in 2024, the tenth consecutive year of below-normal rainfall in much of the archipelago. The crisis reinforced strategic emphasis on desalination, treated wastewater reuse and climate-resilient agriculture.

title: Cocaine Transit Concerns Trigger Security Cooperation
description: Record cocaine seizures in Cabo Verdean waters and ports in 2024 reinforced the country's exposure to South America-Europe trafficking corridors, prompting deepened cooperation with the US Drug Enforcement Administration, Portuguese maritime police and the Maritime Analysis and Operations Centre. Security cooperation remained a central pillar of the EU partnership.

title: Renewable Share Expansion Accelerates
description: New solar and wind capacity additions on Santiago, Sal and São Vicente lifted the renewable share of electricity generation toward 30 percent in 2024, advancing the 2030 target of 50 percent. Battery storage pilots and inter-island grid investments aimed to overcome small-grid integration limits.

title: Legislative and Presidential Elections Scheduled
description: Legislative elections were scheduled for 2026 with presidential elections to follow, with the MpD government of Ulisses Correia e Silva seeking a third mandate against a PAICV in opposition. The campaigns were expected to focus on cost of living, drought resilience, tourism dependence and youth emigration.

title: Diaspora Engagement and Remittance Strategy
description: The government published an updated diaspora engagement strategy in 2025 targeting the roughly half a million Cabo Verdean-origin residents in the United States, Portugal, the Netherlands, France and Senegal, who together send home remittances equivalent to around 12 percent of GDP. New investment incentives, dual nationality streamlining and a diaspora bond programme were proposed.

title: EU Special Partnership Renewed
description: Cabo Verde and the European Union renewed and deepened their Special Partnership framework in 2025 with new strands on green transition financing, blue economy cooperation and digital connectivity, alongside continued mobility and security cooperation. The renewal reaffirmed Praia's strategic alignment with Brussels.

title: Ocean Economy and Atlantic Hub Strategy
description: The government formalised an Atlantic maritime hub strategy in 2025 building on port investments at Praia, Mindelo and Sal Rei to position the archipelago as a logistics, bunkering, cruise and submarine cable junction between Europe, Africa and the Americas. The strategy linked to broader CPLP and ECOWAS frameworks.
